extracted.intended_audience: emerging short-story writers and people researching literary magazines
extracted.subtask_short: submitting short stories to Glimmer Train
extracted.subtask_description: Information about the short-story literary journal Glimmer Train: what it published, its audience, contest structure, selectivity, and editorial preferences relevant to writers considering submission or researching the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content: short stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Glimmer Train was an American short story literary journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal published short fiction (short stories). Submissions should therefore be short story manuscripts suitable for a literary short-fiction journal rather than poetry, novels, or other forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience: emerging writers
rubrics_metrics.description: It was published quarterly, accepting works primarily from emerging writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Glimmer Train prioritized new/emerging voices; writers submitting should consider that the magazine historically sought work from less-established authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selectivity / acceptance rate
rubrics_metrics.description: While the journal received over 40,000 submissions per year, only about 40 stories are published (a rate of 0.001, or 1/10 of 1%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extremely competitive — writers should expect a very low chance of acceptance and prepare submissions accordingly (high polish, strong voice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial preference: 'timeless stories' and 'new voices'
rubrics_metrics.description: Referenced coverage: 'Glimmer Train Wants Timeless Stories From New Voices' (Poets & Writers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial taste reportedly favored stories with a sense of timelessness and fresh perspectives; consider emphasizing universal themes executed with distinct voice and craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contests and prizes
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal held 12 short story fiction contests a year, paying out over $50,000 on an annual basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Much of the magazine's publication and prize distribution occurred via recurring contests — writers could submit to those contests (often a primary route to publication) and should review contest rules, deadlines, and prize structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputation and discoverability
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories published in Glimmer Train were listed in The Best American Short Stories and appeared in the Pushcart Prize, The PEN/O. Henry Prize Stories, and various anthologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication in Glimmer Train historically conferred prestige and visibility; successful submissions could increase chances of selection for year-end anthologies and prizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writer process advice from founder
rubrics_metrics.description: Burmeister-Brown advises writers to: 'Unplug yourself from the hurly-burly of life on a regular basis so your subconscious has time to make some good compost.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical advice for craft and productivity: build regular, distraction-free time for writing to allow ideas to develop subconsciously.
